beats.title: Huffman's term paper and the compression problem
beats.whatChanges: Portraits, exam-vs-paper choice, and text/image/video examples are progressively replaced by bit-count expressions boxed under one question.
beats.invariant: The framing problem statement (represent symbols in the fewest bits) stays on screen as everything else transforms beneath it.

beats.title: Source-encoder-message-decoder-receiver setup and the three requirements
beats.whatChanges: Encoding tables and the encoded 'Shannon' bitstring are ReplacementTransformed through valid, lossy, and ambiguous variants as each requirement is introduced.
beats.invariant: The five-component communication diagram and its arrows stay fixed while only the encoding dictionary and message bits mutate.

beats.title: Redundancy vs information loss on a bit-length scale
beats.whatChanges: A triangle marker slides along a number line of encoded-message length as encodings swap between redundant, lossy, and optimal.
beats.invariant: The number line with its redundancy and information-loss arrows persists, visualizing that a hard lower limit must exist.

beats.title: Measuring information: four axioms force I(x) = -log2 p(x)
beats.whatChanges: Thought-experiment statements give way to a growing list of axioms and then a plotted information-vs-probability curve.
beats.invariant: The axiom list stays visible as the unique function satisfying it is derived and graphed.

beats.title: Entropy as weighted average; biased-coin maximum; the name
beats.whatChanges: Seattle/Phoenix bar charts collapse to H values, then a dot sweeps the biased-coin entropy curve while an updater redraws the bar chart in lockstep.
beats.invariant: The bar-chart probabilities and the curve point always agree, keeping distribution and entropy visibly coupled.

beats.title: Average length per symbol, L >= H(X), and the yes/no question diagram
beats.whatChanges: A sampled symbol stream cascades from the distribution, then a question tree is built top-down and its edge labels transform from yes/no into bits.
beats.invariant: The source distribution and the bound L >= H(X) remain on screen while the question diagram gives the bound operational meaning.

beats.title: Uneven distribution: split into equally likely groups to hit entropy
beats.whatChanges: Sorted probabilities are recursively split with dashed lines and the split groups transform into the earlier question diagram, yielding codes with L exactly H(X).
beats.invariant: Group probability sums stay displayed at each split, and the encoding-length-equals-self-information pattern holds throughout.

beats.title: Shannon-Fano coding, prefix-free codes as full binary trees, suboptimality
beats.whatChanges: Node groups split top-down into a tree, edges are colored 0/1, a message is decoded path-by-path, and a counterexample shows L = 2.31 beaten by 2.30.
beats.invariant: The prefix property is visibly maintained: every symbol stays a leaf with a unique root path while codes and totals are annotated.

beats.title: L as depth-weighted sum; two least likely symbols must sit at the bottom
beats.whatChanges: Depth labels appear on tree edges, then the two lowest-probability leaves are pulled to the bottom under a new parent while remaining symbols are boxed as constrained.
beats.invariant: The formula L = sum of p_i times depth stays pinned at top as concrete numbers and generalized p_1..p_n symbols swap beneath it.

beats.title: L as sum of internal node probabilities; the subproblem recursion
beats.whatChanges: Internal node values are expanded via TransformFromCopy into sums of leaf probabilities, then the cost is rewritten as p1 + p2 + L(merged set), justifying repeated greedy merging.
beats.invariant: The equivalence of the two cost formulations is kept on screen, with colored rectangles tying each formula term to its tree region.

beats.title: Building the Huffman tree by repeated lowest-pair merges
beats.whatChanges: At each step the two lowest nodes move from the sorted column into tree position, edges grow, a parent circle appears, and a copy of the parent re-enters the re-sorted frontier.
beats.invariant: The frontier column stays sorted by probability after every merge, and each parent's displayed value is always the sum of its children.

beats.title: From text to character frequencies to the same merge process
beats.whatChanges: Characters of 'ADBADEDBBDD' fly into per-letter groups, become frequency/key leaf boxes, are sorted, and merge into the full tree.
beats.invariant: Every original character is visibly conserved into exactly one leaf, so leaf frequencies always sum to the text length.

beats.title: Node class plus heapq priority-queue implementation
beats.whatChanges: Syntax-highlighted code for Node and getHuffmanTree is written line-group by line-group beside a picture-in-picture replay of the animation.
beats.invariant: The code mirrors the exact merge loop just animated: pop two minima, push their sum, repeat until one root remains.

beats.title: Top-down Shannon-Fano vs bottom-up Huffman; the story arc
beats.whatChanges: The four requirements return with checkmarks, 'obvious' gets crossed out, and the ideas collapse into an information-theory-to-Huffman progression box.
beats.invariant: The requirement list and the top-down/bottom-up contrast anchor the recap of everything built earlier.
